title: Quiz: Development of the Atomic Model

questions.stem: John Dalton proposed one of the earliest atomic models. What did he suggest atoms were like?

options.text: A cloud of negative charge
A nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons
Tiny solid spheres that could not be divided
A positive sphere with electrons embedded in it

questions.explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms were tiny, solid, indivisible spheres. This was the earliest scientific model of the atom, developed in the early 1800s.

questions.stem: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron and proposed the 'plum pudding' model. What did this model suggest?

options.text: Electrons are embedded in a ball of positive charge
A small positive nucleus is surrounded by orbiting electrons
Electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels
Atoms are solid spheres with no internal structure

questions.explanation: Thomson's plum pudding model proposed that atoms were a sphere of positive charge with negatively charged electrons scattered throughout, like plums in a pudding.

questions.stem: What did Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment reveal about the atom?

options.text: That atoms are indivisible
That most of the atom is empty space with a small, dense, positive nucleus
That neutrons exist in the nucleus
That electrons have a negative charge

questions.explanation: Rutherford found that most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil (empty space), but a few were deflected back. This proved the atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

questions.stem: How did Niels Bohr improve upon Rutherford's model of the atom?

options.text: He discovered the proton
He proved that atoms are indivisible
He discovered that the nucleus contains neutrons
He proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances in fixed energy levels

questions.explanation: Bohr adapted Rutherford's model by suggesting that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances in fixed energy levels (shells), rather than at random distances.

questions.stem: Who discovered the neutron, and when?

options.text: Thomson in 1897
Chadwick in 1932
Bohr in 1913
Rutherford in 1911

questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932. This was the last major subatomic particle to be discovered and completed our basic understanding of atomic structure.

questions.stem: Why do scientific models of the atom change over time?

options.text: Because technology makes atoms easier to see directly
Because new experimental evidence provides better understanding
Because scientists like to disagree with each other
Because older models were completely wrong

questions.explanation: Scientific models are updated when new experimental evidence is discovered that cannot be explained by the existing model. Each new model builds on previous understanding.

questions.stem: Which is the correct chronological order of atomic models?

options.text: Plum pudding, Dalton's sphere, Nuclear, Bohr
Dalton's sphere, Plum pudding, Nuclear, Bohr
Bohr, Nuclear, Plum pudding, Dalton's sphere
Nuclear, Plum pudding, Dalton's sphere, Bohr

questions.explanation: The correct order is: Dalton's solid sphere model (early 1800s), Thomson's plum pudding model (1897), Rutherford's nuclear model (1911), and Bohr's energy level model (1913).
